reading.body:
Zapier is a 13-year-old workflow automation platform that positions AI as a layer on top of plumbing connecting over 9,000 applications, handling the infrastructure that makes multi-app AI agents reliable at scale.

The company's two products sit at different points in the same stack. Zapier AI adds intelligence to existing workflows while managing data governance across 7,000 integrated apps. Zapier Central abstracts away the complexity of coordinating actions across those apps by packaging agentic behavior—lead qualification, ticket routing, autonomous task handling—into managed workflows. Both products delegate authentication, retries, and rate limiting to Zapier's runtime rather than forcing each AI system to solve those problems independently. This matters because AI agents at production scale fail less often when infrastructure handles the plumbing.

The data covers products and platform scope but does not address pricing, customer count, compute requirements, or the power and real estate footprint of Zapier's own infrastructure. It does not indicate whether Zapier's server infrastructure is cloud-hosted, on-premises, or hybrid. For understanding AI scaling constraints, what matters most is that Zapier sits downstream of compute—it optimizes what applications do with compute, not how much compute exists or where it runs.

profile_text.body:
Zapier is a for-profit startup founded in 2011 and described as remote-first. Its AI page presents the company as a unified orchestration platform for adding AI where a customer needs it: inside a workflow, as an agent, or as a customer chatbot. The site frames the central problem not as the AI itself but as connecting it to real tools, running it reliably, and keeping it safe as a team grows.

The company's tracked products are Zapier AI, which it describes as workflow automation with AI, 7000+ app integrations, data flow governance, and cross-app exposure controls, and Zapier Central, which it describes as workflow automation with agentic actions. According to the site, one connection gives an AI access to 30,000+ actions across 9,000+ apps, with Zapier handling authentication, retries, and rate limits. It names Claude, ChatGPT, and Cursor as AI tools that can be plugged in, says AI assistants connect through MCP and developers and coding agents through an SDK, and states that built-in checks catch sensitive data and unsafe inputs before anything is sent or saved. The site also says the runtime is backed by Zapier's 13-year-old production infrastructure, and it includes customer testimonials describing efficiency gains and a multimillion-dollar company built with the platform.

The profile records no lawsuits involving the company.
